formula: pronoun ~ (a + b + c)^3 + ((a + b + c)^3 | subject) + ((a + b)^2 | item)
documented_prior: prior.m3 <- list(R=list(V=1, n=1, fix=1), G=list(G1=list(V=diag(8), n=8, alpha.mu=rep(0, 8), alpha.V=diag(8)*25^2), G2=list(V=diag(4), n=4, alpha.mu=rep(0, 4), alpha.V=diag(4)*25^2)))
notes: OpenClustered language (dat4), from von der Malsburg & Zhan's MCMCglmm-intro README (github.com/tmalsburg/MCMCglmm-intro): a 2x2x2 language-production experiment, 71 subjects and 36 items, pronoun 1 where the description used a pronoun, a and b vary within items and c between items, all coded -1/1. The README fits the maximal model m1 <- glmer(pronoun ~ (a + b + c)^3 + ((a + b + c)^3 | subject) + ((a + b)^2 | item), family="binomial"), which fails to converge, and its MCMCglmm analogue m3/m4: MCMCglmm(pronoun ~ (a + b + c)^3, ~ us(1 + (a + b + c)^3):subject + us(1 + (a + b)^2):item, family = "categorical", prior = prior.m3), m4 with nitt 23000, burnin 3000 and thin 20. The formula is that lme4 rendering; the slopes of the interactions stay in the formula only. RULE GAP: MCMCglmm's categorical family is a logit with a residual variance fixed at 1, an observation-level effect the contract's logit does not carry.

formula: SUFlike ~ Gender + ConversationType + Priming + (1 | ID)
notes: OpenClustered irishenglish (dat5), from LADAL's mixed-effects binomial logistic regression (ladal.edu.au/regression.html, now tutorials/mixedmodel/mixedmodel.html): speech units of 208 speakers (ID), SUFlike 1 where the unit ends in discourse like. After a glmulti search by BIC over Gender, Age, ConversationType and Priming with (1 | ID), the minimal adequate model is mlr.glmer <- glmer(SUFlike ~ (1 | ID) + Gender + ConversationType + Priming, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")); Age dropped out and stays usable.

formula: tapped ~ speechrate + syntax + (1 + syntax + speechrate || participant) + (1 + syntax + speechrate || item)
notes: OpenClustered tapping (dat6): Kilbourn-Ceron et al. (2017) /t/-tapping production data, the McGill LING 620 subset on OSF 8rjxu (nonce words before a vowel-initial word, syntax transitive or intransitive crossed with speech rate). Sonderegger's Regression Modeling for Linguistic Data (people.linguistics.mcgill.ca/~morgan/qmld-book/), chapter 8, exercise 1 (mixed-effects-logistic-regression.html): ex1.mod <- glmer(tapped ~ speechrate.slow + syntax.trans + (1 + syntax.trans + speechrate.slow||participant) + (1 + syntax.trans + speechrate.slow||item), family="binomial"), after dropping the rows with tapped missing; syntax.trans and speechrate.slow are arm::rescale() of syntax and speechrate (+-0.5). released, vowelduration, segmentAfterDuration and pause are other acoustic outcomes of the same production (vowelduration is model 2's response); file and text name the recording and the item's sentence.

formula: vowelduration ~ syntax * speechrate + (1 + syntax * speechrate || item) + (1 + syntax * speechrate || participant)
notes: Sonderegger's qmld-book, chapter 7 exercise on the tapping data (lmem.html, section 7.13): the solution model is vowelduration ~ syntax.trans * speechrate.slow + (1 + syntax.trans * speechrate.slow || item) + (1 + syntax.trans * speechrate.slow || participant), the predictors rescaled to +-0.5; the book takes vowel duration as a proxy for juncture strength. The slopes of the interaction stay in the formula only.

formula: prominence ~ context + (1 + context || item) + (1 + context || participant)
notes: OpenClustered alternatives (dat7): Wagner (2016) prominence-shift production data, the McGill LING 620 subset on OSF dha2j, every item read in the three contexts New, NoAlternative and Alternative. Sonderegger's qmld-book, chapter 8 (mixed-effects-logistic-regression.html), fits alternativesMod2 <- glmer(shifted ~ context + (1+context1+context2||item) + (1+context1+context2||participant), family="binomial", bobyqa), shifted being 1 where prominence is Adjective and context1, context2 the numeric contrasts of context; chapter 9 fits the same model on prominence. The node's givrep.R fits the handbook chapter's correlated version, glmer(annot~Context+(Context|item)+(Context|participant), family="binomial"), on the node's full alternatives.csv. rpitch, rintensity and rduration are the acoustic outcomes (rintensity and rpitch are models 2 and 3); text is the item's passage.

formula: rintensity ~ context + (context | participant) + (context | item)
notes: Wagner's givrep.R on OSF dha2j, the code behind the handbook chapter's table of RelIntensity, RelPitch and ProminenceShift: modelintensity=lmer(rintensity~Context+(Context|participant)+(Context|item),data=data), rintensity being the maximum intensity of the adjective minus that of the noun. The script fits the node's full alternatives.csv (data.csv), of which this file is the course subset, with the level spelled "No Alternative"; hence medium.

formula: rpitch ~ context + (context | participant) + (context | item)
notes: Wagner's givrep.R on OSF dha2j: modelpitch=lmer(rpitch~Context+(Context|participant)+(Context|item),data=data), rpitch being the maximum pitch of the adjective minus that of the noun; an earlier fit rpitch~Context*order with full slopes fails to converge. Fitted on the node's full alternatives.csv, of which this file is the course subset; hence medium.

formula: stressshift ~ conditionLabel + npType + voice + (1 + conditionLabel + npType || item) + (1 + conditionLabel + npType + voice || participant)
notes: OpenClustered givenness (dat8): Wagner (2012) "A givenness illusion", the McGill LING 620 subset on OSF r4j2w, a 2x2 within-item Latin-square production experiment (conditionLabel Contrast or Williams, npType full or pronoun). Sonderegger's qmld-book, chapter 8, model 1 (mixed-effects-logistic-regression.html, section 8.2.1): lrMod1 <- glmer(stressshift ~ clabel.williams + npType.pron + voice.passive + (1 + clabel.williams + npType.pron||item) + (1 + clabel.williams + npType.pron + voice.passive||participant), family="binomial", bobyqa), the predictors arm::rescale()d to +-0.5; voice varies between items, so it has no by-item slope. condition codes the four conditionLabel x npType cells; acoustics is model 2's response.

formula: acoustics ~ conditionLabel * npType + voice + order + (1 + conditionLabel * npType + voice || participant) + (1 + conditionLabel * npType || item)
notes: Sonderegger's qmld-book, chapter 7 (lmem.html, section 7.6.3), model 3B: mod3b <- lmer(acoustics ~ conditionLabel.williams*npType.pron + voice.passive + order.std + (1 + conditionLabel.williams*npType.pron + voice.passive || participant) + (1 + conditionLabel.williams*npType.pron || item), data=givenness), the predictors rescaled; the chapter's simpler fits (mod2a, mod3a, mod1c.not) nest in it. acoustics is a constructed linear predictor of the acoustic cues to prominence, which the book's appendix says not to use for replication. The slopes of the interaction stay in the formula only.

formula: acc ~ sleep_wake * session + (1 + sleep_wake | ID) + (1 + sleep_wake | item)
notes: OpenClustered memory (dat11): Emma James's YSJ R workshop, its mixed-effects lesson (emljames.github.io/YSJ_R_workshop/mixed-effects.html, mixed-effects.Rmd), on children's picture naming of newly learned words after a sleep or a wake interval (James, Gaskell & Henderson 2020), tested in session 1 and 2. The lesson's accuracy model is mem_acc_2 <- glmer(acc ~ sleep_wake*session + (1+sleep_wake|ID) + (1+sleep_wake|item), family = "binomial", data = pn_long), with sleep_wake and session sum-coded factors; its exercises find that only sleep_wake slopes can be added, and mem_acc_v1 adds the standardized vocab on the rows with vocab, which stays usable. RT is model 2's response.

formula: I(1/RT) ~ sleep_wake * session + (1 + sleep_wake | ID) + (1 | item)
notes: The lesson's response-time model after its residual check: pn_long$RT_inv <- 1/pn_long$RT; mem_rt_inv <- lmer(RT_inv ~ sleep_wake*session + (1+sleep_wake|ID) + (1|item), data = pn_long). RT is in ms and recorded on accurate trials only; the exercises add by-item sleep_wake and session slopes (mem_rt_inv2, mem_rt_inv3).

formula: level ~ luck + heterogeneity + (1 | participant)
notes: OpenClustered study1.data (dat20): Nettle & Saxe, preferences for redistribution, study 1 (OSF xrqae, master data analysis.r; Nettle's bookdown chapter is gone): each participant sets the preferred level of redistribution in six vignettes crossing luck (Low, Medium, High) with heterogeneity. The script fits m1 = lmer(level~luck+heterogeneity + (1|participant), REML=T, data=d1), luck leveled Low, Medium, High and heterogeneity with Homogeneous as reference; m1b and m1c add left.right and SDO. mode, the preferred mode of redistribution, is model 2's response; level.relative and level.within.subjects.centred are derived from level; Unnamed: 0 numbers the rows.

formula: mode ~ luck + heterogeneity + (1 | participant)
notes: Nettle & Saxe's master data analysis.r, models for the mode of redistribution, study 1: mode1 = lmer(mode~luck+heterogeneity + (1|participant), REML=T, data=d1); mode1b and mode1c add left.right and SDO.

formula: frequency ~ attitude + gender + (1 + attitude | subject) + (1 + attitude | scenario)
notes: OpenClustered politeness (dat22): Winter (2013), "Linear models and linear mixed effects models in R", tutorial 2 (bodowinter.com/tutorial/bw_LME_tutorial2.pdf), on Winter & Grawunder (2012): the voice pitch (frequency, Hz) of Korean speakers (subject) in polite and informal attitude across scenarios (the items). The tutorial builds from lmer(frequency ~ attitude + gender + (1|subject) + (1|scenario)) to the random-slope model politeness.model = lmer(frequency ~ attitude + gender + (1+attitude|subject) + (1+attitude|scenario), data=politeness, REML=FALSE). One row lacks frequency.

formula: HT ~ DBH + (1 | CoverType/PlotNum)
notes: OpenClustered redpine (dat30): Russell's stats4nr (stats4nr.com/linear-mixed-models; package data redpine), red pine trees on forest inventory plots of the Cloquet Forestry Center, Minnesota, 2014, height HT (ft) on diameter DBH (in). The chapter compares redpine.lme (1 | CoverType), redpine.lme2 (1 + DBH | CoverType, singular) and the recommended redpine.lme3 <- lmer(HT ~ DBH + (1 | CoverType/PlotNum), data = redpine), 124 plots nested in 13 cover types, lowest AIC. Plot numbers are unique across cover types, so PlotNum is the inner factor. TreeNum numbers the tree.

formula: final_result ~ gender + region + highest_education + imd_band + age_band + num_of_prev_attempts + studied_credits + disability + (1 | code_module:code_presentation) + (1 | id_student)
notes: OULAD (Kuzilek, Hlosta & Zdrahal 2017, Sci Data 4:170171; UCI 349 and its OULAD.names): one row per student registered on a module presentation (seven modules, 22 presentations), final_result Distinction, Pass, Fail or Withdrawn. Data Foundry's record (open_university_learning_analytics_dataset) builds a day-60 final_result task from the joined tables, holds out whole presentations and flags students who recur across registrations. No mixed model is published; the random intercepts per module presentation and per student on the codebook's demographic columns are the reader's proposal.

formula: sum_click ~ date + (1 | id_student) + (1 | id_site)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: OULAD studentVle (Kuzilek et al. 2017; OULAD.names): one row per student, VLE material and day, sum_click the number of the student's interactions with the material that day; students repeat across materials and days, materials across students. Neither the source nor Data Foundry's record, which turns the clicks into features, models them; the count on the day with crossed intercepts per student and material is the reader's proposal. code_module and code_presentation name the module presentation each material belongs to.

formula: FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_LITHOLOGY ~ DEPTH_MD + GROUP + CALI + RMED + RDEP + RHOB + GR + NPHI + PEF + DTC + SP + DRHO + (1 | WELL)
notes: FORCE 2020 lithology competition (Bormann et al. 2020, github.com/bolgebrygg/Force-2020-Machine-Learning-competition, readme.md and lithology_competition/): wireline logs at depth steps down the training wells of the Norwegian shelf, the target FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_LITHOLOGY a lithology code scored by a 12 x 12 penalty matrix, with NPD's GROUP and FORMATION picks and the well position given as features. Data Foundry's record (force_2020_...) splits by well and declares the depth order within a well. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per well on depth, GROUP and the widely logged curves is the reader's proposal. FORMATION and the sparsely logged curves (RSHA, SGR, BS, ROP, DTS, DCAL, MUDWEIGHT, RMIC, ROPA, RXO) stay usable; X_LOC, Y_LOC and Z_LOC are coordinates and FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_CONFIDENCE is the interpreter's confidence in the label.

formula: TL ~ TR + (1 | TREE) + (1 | TREE:BR)
notes: Camacho & Arron (1995), Canadian Journal of Statistics case study (OpenML 23380 cjs): trimmed silver maple trees trunk-injected with paclobutrazol or flurprimidol at two rates or kept as two controls (TR), ten trees per set, six to eight limbs (BR) cut per tree and every terminal sprout measured: total length TL (cm, sprouts of 1 cm or less recorded as 1) and number of internodes IN (model 2). Data Foundry's record (cjs) notes that sprouts repeat within tree. Branch letters restart per tree, so the limb is TREE:BR, and sprouts 1868 to 1879 lack a branch. The case study's analysis is not stated; the random intercepts per tree and limb are the reader's proposal. INTERNODE_1 to INTERNODE_29 hold each sprout's internode lengths, wide; N numbers the sprout.

formula: IN ~ TR + (1 | TREE) + (1 | TREE:BR)
notes: The study's second response, the number of internodes per sprout, on the same design; the random intercepts per tree and limb are the reader's proposal.

formula: runtime ~ algorithm + stacks + tiers + stack.tier.ratio + container.density + empty.stack.pct + overstowing.stack.pct + overstowing.2cont.stack.pct + group.same.min + group.same.max + group.same.mean + group.same.stdev + top.good.min + top.good.max + top.good.mean + top.good.stdev + overstowage.pct + bflb + left.density + tier.weighted.groups + avg.l1.top.left.lg.group + cont.empty.grt.estack + pct.bottom.pct.on.top + (1 | instance_id)
notes: CPMP-2015 algorithm-selection scenario (OpenML 41700; ASlib, Tierney & Malitsky features, Tierney, Pacino & Voss algorithms): the runtime of four A* and IDA* variants (algorithm) on each container pre-marshalling instance (instance_id), with the instance's latent-feature-analysis features repeated on its rows. Data Foundry's record (cpmp_2015_...) calls for a split grouped by instance. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per instance with the algorithm and the instance features as fixed effects is the reader's proposal; runstatus (ok, timeout, memout) restates the runtime. RULE GAP: runtimes stop at the 3600 s cutoff on timeouts and memouts and span orders of magnitude down to zero, and the rules settle neither the censoring nor a log scale.

formula: PAR10 ~ algorithm + (1 | instance_id)
notes: MIP-2016 algorithm-selection scenario (OpenML 43071; Bergdoll, Open Algorithm Challenge 2017): PAR10 runtimes of five MIP solvers (algorithm) on each solvable MIPLIB2010 instance (instance_id), from Mittelmann's 12-thread benchmarks, with the instance's EPM features repeated on its rows. Data Foundry's record (mip_2016_...) notes that algorithm selection needs a split grouped by instance. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per instance with the solver as fixed effect is the reader's proposal, and the instance features, too many for the instances, stay usable. RULE GAP: PAR10 scores a timeout as ten times the cutoff, so the response mixes runtimes with a penalty, and the rules settle neither that nor a log scale.

formula: Class ~ Bidder_Tendency + Bidding_Ratio + Successive_Outbidding + Last_Bidding + Auction_Bids + Starting_Price_Average + Early_Bidding + Winning_Ratio + Auction_Duration + (1 | Auction_ID) + (1 | Bidder_ID)
notes: Shill Bidding Dataset (Alzahrani & Sadaoui 2018; UCI 562): one row per bidder in a scraped eBay auction, eight shill-bidding features computed per bidder or per auction, Class 1 for shill behaviour. Data Foundry's record (shill_bidding_dataset) proposes splits grouped by auction and bidder. No mixed model is published; crossed random intercepts per auction and bidder are the reader's proposal. Bidder_ID is masked to its first and last characters but documented as a unique identifier; Record_ID numbers the rows.

formula: `No-show` ~ Gender + Age + Scholarship + Hipertension + Diabetes + Alcoholism + Handcap + SMS_received + (1 | PatientId) + (1 | Neighbourhood)
notes: Medical Appointment No Shows (Kaggle joniarroba/noshowappointments, Hoppen, Aquarela Analytics): medical appointments in Vitoria, Brazil, 2016, No-show Yes where the patient missed it; patients (PatientId) book several appointments and Neighbourhood is where the appointment takes place. Data Foundry's record (medical_noshow_appointments) asks for grouped splits. No mixed model is published; random intercepts per patient and neighbourhood are the reader's proposal. ScheduledDay and AppointmentDay are timestamps loaded as text and AppointmentID numbers the appointments.

formula: dec ~ attr + intel + amb + gender + attr:gender + intel:gender + amb:gender + (1 | iid) + (1 | pid)
notes: Fisman, Iyengar, Kamenica & Simonson (2006), QJE 121:673-697, the Columbia speed-dating experiment in 21 waves (Kaggle annavictoria/speed-dating-experiment and its Speed Dating Data Key): one row per participant (iid) and partner met (pid), dec the participant's yes or no. Table III fits Decision_ij = alpha_i + sum_c beta_c Rating_ijc + e_ij on the participant's ratings of the partner's attractiveness, intelligence and ambition (attr, intel, amb): a linear probability model with participant fixed effects, standard errors clustered by partner and weights 1/NumberOfPartners, column 3 pooling both genders with Rating*Male interactions; the paper reports similar results by conditional logit. The participant effect as a random intercept and the partner clustering as a crossed one are the reader's rendering on the contract's logit. id, idg and partner are within-wave numbers; match and dec_o hold the partner's decision.

formula: difficulty ~ instr + nb.repeat + attendance + (1 | class)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Turkiye Student Evaluation (Gunduz & Fokoue, UCI 262): end-of-course evaluations by students of Gazi University, Ankara, in 13 courses (class) of 3 instructors (instr), with the student's number of attempts (nb.repeat), attendance (0-4), perceived difficulty (1-5) and 28 Likert items. UCI names no target, and Data Foundry's record (turkiye_student_evaluation) finds none for prediction but notes the grouping by instructor and course. Perceived difficulty with a random intercept per course is the reader's proposal; the instructor is a three-level covariate, and Q1 to Q28 are the other answers of the same form.

formula: Score ~ Trellis * Method + Position + (1 | Judges) + (1 | Judges:Occasion:Interval:Sittings) + (1 | Squares:Rows:Columns) + (1 | Squares:Rows:Columns:Halfplot)
notes: Brien & Payne's two-phase wine experiment (OpenML 546 sensory; Brien & Payne 1999, The Statistician 48:41-52): in the field phase four trellis types on main plots laid out in two Youden squares of rows and columns, two pruning methods on the halfplots; in the tasting phase six judges scored the halfplots' wines over two occasions of three intervals of four sittings, four glasses (Position) per sitting. Data Foundry's record (sensory) would group by judges and plots. The source analyses the scores by a multi-tiered analysis of variance from structure formulae, not read here; the random intercepts per judge, judge sitting, main plot and halfplot are the reader's rendering of its units.

formula: binaryClass ~ zon_winds + mer_winds + humidity + air_temp + (1 | buoy) + (1 | day)
notes: kdd_el_nino-small, binarized (OpenML 839; the UCI El Nino data of NOAA's Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory): daily readings of moored buoys in the equatorial Pacific, binaryClass P where version 1's numeric target lies below its mean. Data Foundry's record (el_nino_dataset) notes the groups of sensors and the time order. No model is documented; crossed random intercepts per buoy and day are the reader's proposal. latitude and longitude are the buoy's position.

formula: class ~ Alg_Name + (1 | DS_Name)
notes: StatLog meta-data (Brazdil & Gama, LIACC 1996; OpenML 566 meta): the normalized error (class, Norm_error in the codebook) of the StatLog algorithms (Alg_Name) on each StatLog dataset (DS_Name), with the dataset's characteristics (T to NSRatio) repeated on its rows. Data Foundry's records (meta, meta_data) call for a split grouped by dataset. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per dataset with the algorithm as fixed effect is the reader's proposal, and the dataset characteristics stay usable.

formula: Score ~ Season + Age + Pos1 + Conference + Role + G + GS + MP + PTS + TRB + AST + STL + BLK + TOV + mean_views + (1 | Player_ID) + (1 | Tm)
notes: NBA players 2016-2019 (Kaggle davra98/nba-players-20162019, a university project in Milan): one row per player and season, Score the All-Star score, the ranks of the fan, player and media votes weighted 0.5, 0.25 and 0.25. Data Foundry's record (nba_players_2016_2019) groups by player, who appears in up to three seasons, and found that in 2017-18 and 2018-19 Score gives players without player or media votes the ballot size plus one as rank. No mixed model is published; random intercepts per player and team (Tm) on season-long statistics are the reader's proposal. Rk is basketball-reference's row number, Player.x the name, the vote counts and ranks build Score, and Play is the All-Star selection.

formula: Rating ~ `Rating Agency Name` + Sector + currentRatio + quickRatio + cashRatio + daysOfSalesOutstanding + netProfitMargin + pretaxProfitMargin + grossProfitMargin + operatingProfitMargin + returnOnAssets + returnOnCapitalEmployed + returnOnEquity + assetTurnover + fixedAssetTurnover + debtEquityRatio + debtRatio + effectiveTaxRate + freeCashFlowOperatingCashFlowRatio + freeCashFlowPerShare + cashPerShare + companyEquityMultiplier + ebitPerRevenue + enterpriseValueMultiple + operatingCashFlowPerShare + operatingCashFlowSalesRatio + payablesTurnover + (1 | Symbol)
notes: Corporate Credit Rating (Kaggle agewerc/corporate-credit-rating, built by github.com/Agewerc/ML-Finance from opendatasoft ratings and Financial Modeling Prep ratios): ratings AAA to D issued by major agencies to US firms in 2010-2016, one row per rating with the firm's financial ratios. Data Foundry's record (corporate_credit_rating) groups by company and notes that the labels mix issuer with bond and loan ratings. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per firm (Symbol) with agency, sector and ratios as fixed effects is the reader's proposal. Name duplicates Symbol and Date is text. RULE GAP: Rating is text, so its loaded (sorted) level order is not the scale AAA > AA > A > BBB > BB > B > CCC > CC > C > D.

formula: Credit_Score ~ Month + Occupation + Monthly_Inhand_Salary + Num_Bank_Accounts + Num_Credit_Card + Interest_Rate + Delay_from_due_date + Num_Credit_Inquiries + Credit_Mix + Credit_Utilization_Ratio + Payment_of_Min_Amount + Total_EMI_per_month + Payment_Behaviour + (1 | Customer_ID)
notes: Credit score classification (Kaggle parisrohan/credit-score-classification): monthly records, January to August, of bank customers (Customer_ID), Credit_Score Good, Standard or Poor. The page states the task, not the data's origin; Data Foundry's record (credit_score_classification) suspects the table is synthetic, which no source says. The grouping by customer is read from the columns, and the random intercept per customer on the columns that load as numbers or levels is the reader's proposal. Age, Annual_Income, Num_of_Loan, Num_of_Delayed_Payment, Changed_Credit_Limit, Outstanding_Debt, Amount_invested_monthly and Monthly_Balance are numbers corrupted with text (trailing underscores, sentinels), Credit_History_Age and Type_of_Loan are free text, and ID, Name and SSN identify the row and the person. RULE GAP: Credit_Score is text, so its loaded (sorted) level order is not Poor < Standard < Good.

formula: label ~ fixcount + firstPassCnt + P1stFixation + P2stFixation + prevFixDur + firstfixDur + firstPassFixDur + nextFixDur + firstSaccLen + lastSaccLen + prevFixPos + landingPos + leavingPos + totalFixDur + meanFixDur + nRegressFrom + regressLen + nextWordRegress + regressDur + pupilDiamMax + pupilDiamLag + timePrtctg + (1 | assgNo)
notes: Inferring relevance from eye movements, challenge 2005 (Salojarvi et al., HUT report A82; OpenML 1044 eye_movements): each assignment (assgNo) is a question followed by ten news titles, one correct (2), four relevant (1) and five irrelevant (0); each row is one word read, with 22 eye-movement features, and label is its title's class. Data Foundry's record (eye_movements) notes the groups. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per assignment on the word features is the reader's proposal. lineNo numbers the rows; titleNo, wordNo and nWordsInTitle place the word. RULE GAP: label is constant within each title (assgNo:titleNo), whose words repeat it, and every assignment holds the same mix of title classes by design, so only the assignment can carry a random effect and it can vary little.
